<b>Подъязычная кость</b> — подкова над г: Hyoid bone — a horseshoe above the larynx and the only bone with no joint to any other bone: it hangs on muscles and ligaments. The larynx is suspended from it by the thyrohyoid membrane, and the muscles of the tongue and the floor of the mouth attach to it from above.
<b>Перстневидный хрящ</b> — единственное: Cricoid cartilage — the only complete cartilage ring of the airway. It is shaped like a signet ring: a narrow arch in front and a tall plate — the “signet” — behind. The arytenoid cartilages sit on that plate, and the thyroid cartilage joins it on each side.
<b>Черпаловидные хрящи</b> — парные пира: Arytenoid cartilages — paired little pyramids on the cricoid plate (with tiny corniculate cartilages on top). The vocal process points forward and holds the vocal fold; the muscular process points sideways, and muscles pull on it. By rotating and sliding, the cartilages open and close the glottis.
<b>Надгортанник</b> — гибкий лепесток из: Epiglottis — a flexible leaf of elastic cartilage behind the root of the tongue. When you swallow, the larynx rises toward it, it tips over and covers the entrance to the larynx, and food goes into the esophagus. Swallow and laugh at the same time, and a crumb may slip past — then you cough.
<b>Голосовые складки</b> — голосовая свя: Vocal folds — the vocal ligament and the vocalis muscle under the mucosa, stretched from the angle of the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoids. The gap between them is the glottis, the narrowest part of the adult airway. Above them lie the vestibular (“false”) folds.
<b>Трахея</b> начинается от перстневидно: The trachea starts at the cricoid cartilage: 16–20 cartilage half-rings open at the back. The back wall is muscle and connective tissue; the esophagus lies against it, and a swallowed bite can push it in a little.
<b>Глубокий вдох.</b> Задние перстнечерп: Deep breath in. The posterior cricoarytenoid muscles — the only ones that open the glottis — pull the muscular processes back, and the arytenoids swing their vocal processes outward. The glottis becomes a wide triangle, more than a centimeter across at its base.
<b>Спокойное дыхание.</b> Мышцы почти не: Quiet breathing. The muscles barely work: the glottis is a narrow open triangle and narrows a little when you breathe out.
<b>Шёпот.</b> Складки сомкнуты спереди,: Whisper. The folds touch in front, but a triangular gap stays open between the arytenoid cartilages. Air rushes through with a hiss and the folds do not vibrate — a sound without pitch.
<b>Гортань</b> — хрящевая коробка в нача: The larynx is a box of cartilage at the start of the airway: it lets air through, shuts the way into the trachea when you swallow, and makes the voice. Its frame is three unpaired cartilages (thyroid, cricoid, epiglottis) and three paired ones (arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform). Click a cartilage or pick it below.
<b>Высота голоса.</b> Перстнещитовидная: Pitch. The cricothyroid muscle tips the thyroid cartilage forward and down — it rotates at the cricothyroid joint. The folds get longer and tighter and vibrate faster, so the voice goes up. The vocalis muscle inside the fold does the opposite: it shortens and relaxes them. Loudness comes from how hard you breathe out.
Хрящевая коробка размером с грецкий орех: A box of cartilage the size of a walnut: it opens the way for air, snaps shut when you swallow, and turns your breath into a voice — two folds of mucosa vibrating hundreds of times a second.
\n <div><h2>Строение</h2>\n:
Structure

The larynx lies at the level of the 4th–6th cervical vertebrae, below the hyoid bone and above the trachea. Its frame: the thyroid and cricoid cartilages and the epiglottis (unpaired), and the arytenoid, corniculate and cuneiform cartilages (paired). The cartilages are linked by joints (cricothyroid and cricoarytenoid), ligaments and membranes.

Inside there are three levels: the vestibule (above the vestibular folds), the middle part with the vocal folds, and the subglottic space that leads into the trachea. Nerve supply comes from the vagus nerve: the superior laryngeal nerve (sensation and the cricothyroid muscle) and the recurrent laryngeal nerve (all the other muscles).

How the voice is made

The source is the folds: airflow pushes the closed folds apart, their elasticity and the suction of the fast flow close them again, about 100–130 times a second in men and about 200–220 in women. That is a buzz without words. Words come from the “filter” — the throat, mouth and nose: the tongue and lips change the shape of these spaces and boost different overtones, which gives the vowels.

Men’s folds are longer (17–25 mm versus 12–17 mm), so their voices are lower. In puberty, testosterone makes a boy’s larynx grow fast and the folds lengthen — the voice “breaks” and drops by almost an octave.

Medicine

  • Hoarseness is a common sign of laryngitis. If it lasts longer than 2–3 weeks, see an ENT doctor: this is how nodules, polyps and laryngeal cancer (almost always in smokers) show up.
  • Vocal fold nodules are “calluses” in singers, teachers and children who shout a lot.
  • Recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy — the fold on the injured side stops moving and the voice turns husky. The nerve runs next to the thyroid gland (a risk in thyroid surgery), and the left one loops around the aortic arch in the chest.
  • Cricothyrotomy is an emergency cut through the cricothyroid ligament (between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages) when the airway above is blocked.
  • A foreign body most often gets stuck at the glottis, the narrowest point. First aid is the Heimlich maneuver.

Simplifications

  • The cartilages, ligaments and muscles are built schematically after the atlas, without the mucosa, vestibular folds, vessels and nerves; the cuneiform cartilages are not shown.
  • The fold vibration is slowed down tens of times; the frequency in “Pitch” mode is an illustration: in reality it also depends on the mass of the folds and the air pressure below them. The tilt of the thyroid cartilage is exaggerated for clarity.

<b>Щитовидный хрящ</b> — самый крупный:: Thyroid cartilage — the largest one: two plates fused in front at an angle. In men the angle is sharper (about 90°) and the ridge shows on the neck — the Adam’s apple; in women it is about 120°. Like a shield, it covers the vocal folds, which attach to its inner angle. A notch is clearly visible on its upper edge — the superior thyroid notch.
<b>Голос.</b> Латеральные перстнечерпало: Voice. The lateral cricoarytenoid and transverse arytenoid muscles bring the folds together, and the vocalis muscle inside each fold sets how stiff it is. Exhaled air pushes them apart; their elasticity and the suction of the fast airflow close them again — hundreds of times a second. Each opening is a puff of pressure, and that is sound (the vibration is slowed down here).
